newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada oil drillers predict record 1997 wells.
newsitem.headline: Canada oil drillers predict record 1997 wells.

text.p: The Canadian Association of Oilwell Drilling Contractors said on Friday it boosted its forecast for oil and gas wells to be drilled in western Canada this year to a record 14,300.
The projection is 11 percent higher than the CAODC's October forecast for 1997 and 13 percent above the record 12,695 wells drilled in western Canada last year.

"Reasonable commodity prices, rising demand for equipment running through the balance of this year and into the winter drilling season, have caused us to revise our forecast," Duane Mather, president of Nabors Industries Inc unit Nabors Drilling Ltd, said. Mather is the new CAODC president.
He said the association projected the average number of rigs drilling in western Canada to rise to 362 in 1997, up from 316 in 1996. The number would be the highest since 1979-80.
The Canadian drilling fleet, which now numbers 484 rigs, was project to run at an average 72 percent during 1997, up from 66 percent in 1996 and 59 percent in 1995, the CAODC said.
